THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, JANUARY 24, 1925

Move Is Launched For
Release Of Russians
Interned At Arsenal

30 Men Arrested By General Chi Hsieh-yuen's
Agents As 'Spies' Believed Facing Death
Penalty; Freedom Is Sought

Efforts are being made on the part of local Russian newspapers, business firms and other organizations for the immediate release of 30 Russians arrested by General Chi Hsieh-yuen's men on the charge that they are spies acting for the interests of General Lu.

The men are now being held at the Arsenal and it is feared that orders have been issued for their them to be shot. An appeal has been made, it is understood, through the local English newspapers asking them to defend the interests of the Russian refugees.

The following is a translation on the situation as commented upon in 'Russia' a Shanghai newspaper printed yesterday:

"The arrest of Russian piece goods dealers in provinces of China is now being carried out by order of General Chi Hsieh-yuen. The arrested men are accused of 'espionage' in favor of General Lu.

"They have all been sent to the arsenal under strict escort and with bound hands. There are now about 30 Russian prisoners.

"It is not known what their fate will be, but the very fact that they are in the arsenal speaks for itself.

"Some of the men arrested are citizens of U.S.S.R. and have been registered at the local Red Consulate, but the majority are soldiers and members of the Ural-Siberian Labor Company who for a year and a half have been earning their living selling piece goods on behalf of wholesale firms such as 'Voyageur' and 'S. Heumann & Co.' from whom they have received goods and a trade certificate in order to obtain a passport from Chinese authorities.

"The action of General Chi has caused great surprise because he now sees a 'spy' in every Russian employed in peaceful labor and sends them to the arsenal for execution.

"We are waiting from all Russian public organizations and the firms whose goods these people are

selling, a most emphatic solicitation for the release of these Russians who were arrested, although innocent, and to save them from execution.

"The Editor of 'Russia' has on his part sent an appeal to the foreign community through the local English newspapers requesting them to defend the helpless Russian refugees and has also made an emphatic protest against the thoughtless actions of the Chinese general."

30 ARRESTED, CLAIM

The following is a translation of an editorial in the New Shanghai Life:

"Only a few days ago a report announcing the formation of a "White" detachment attached to Marshal Lu's army was published in local newspapers. They were said to be taking active part in the present civil war and now besides confirmation of this report the direct results of fresh "White" activities have become apparent.

"During the past few days over 30 Russians have been arrested by the Chinese authorities and taking into consideration the fact that a war is on there is no fear for their fate. It is difficult to ascertain who these Russians are but no doubt the majority of them if not all have no connection with the new "White" adventure and their arrest is a result of the misunderstanding and the outcome of indignation and anger against Russians, a feeling which prevails now amongst the Chinese people and military officials, thanks to the efforts of the "White" leaders.

《字林西报》，1925年1月24日，星期六

发起运动要求
释放拘禁在兵工厂的俄国人

谢协元将军的手下以“间谍”罪名逮捕了30人，据信面临死刑；寻求自由

当地俄文报纸、商行及其他组织正努力促使立即释放被谢协元将军手下逮捕的30名俄国人，指控他们是代表卢将军利益行事的间谍。

这些人目前被关押在兵工厂，令人担忧的是，处决他们的命令已经下达。据悉，已通过当地英文报纸发出呼吁，请求它们捍卫俄国难民的利益。

以下是昨日出版的上海俄文报纸《俄罗斯报》（Russia）对局势评论的译文：

“中国各省的俄国布匹商人正根据谢协元将军的命令遭到逮捕。被捕者被指控为有利于卢将军的‘间谍’活动。

“他们均在严密押送下手脚被缚，送往兵工厂。目前约有30名俄国囚犯。

“他们的命运尚不可知，但他们身处兵工厂这一事实本身就说明了一切。

“被捕者中有些是苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟公民，并已在当地红色领事馆登记，但大多数是乌拉尔-西伯利亚劳动公司（Ural-Siberian Labor Company）的士兵和成员，他们在过去一年半里代表‘沃亚热尔’（Voyageur）和‘S. Heumann & Co.’等批发商行售卖布匹谋生，并从这些商行获得货物及贸易证明书，以便从中国当局获取护照。

“谢将军的行动引起了极大震惊，因为他现在将每一位从事和平劳动的俄国人视为‘间谍’，并将他们送往兵工厂处决。

“我们等待所有俄国公共组织以及这些人为其
（续至第7页）

（续自第1页）
销售货物的商行发出最强烈的恳求，要求释放这些虽无辜却被捕的俄国人，使他们免遭处决。

“《俄罗斯报》编辑已代表各方通过当地英文报纸向外国侨民社区发出呼吁，请求他们保护无助的俄国难民，并对这位中国将军的轻率行动提出强烈抗议。”

声称逮捕30人

以下是《新上海生活》（New Shanghai Life）一篇社论的译文：

“就在几天前，当地报纸刊登了一则消息，宣布卢元帅麾下组建了一支‘白俄’分队。据说他们积极参与当前的内战，如今除了证实这一报道外，新的‘白俄’活动的直接后果也已显现。

“在过去几天里，中国当局逮捕了30多名俄国人，考虑到战争正在进行，对他们的命运无需担忧。很难查明这些俄国人的身份，但毫无疑问，即使不是全部，其中大多数人也与新的‘白俄’冒险行动毫无关联，他们的逮捕是由于误解所致，也是中国人和军方官员中普遍存在的对俄国人的愤慨和愤怒情绪的结果，而这要归功于‘白俄’领导人的推波助澜。”
